steps.content: Hi there. I'm assisting the inspector in investigating the Sleepwalkers.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Hi. I'm a physician from the neighborhood clinic. I used to work for the laboratory of the District 14 Public Security Bureau. The ex-inspector and I used to be colleagues.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: No need to know my name. I'm here to give you some clues. As half a <color=#fb9259>Sleepwalker</color> myself, I hope I can bring some progress to this stalled case.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Yeah. Because of my work, I've come into contact with some Sleepwalkers and have a rough idea of their illness... If you can call it an "illness," that is.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Plus, not long ago, I also started showing some of the symptoms.

steps.speaker: Options (loop)
options: Did a Sinner do something to you?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: In addition to vomiting the infamous black goo, Sleepwalkers also suffer from uncontrollable lethargy, intermittent memory loss, dispiritedness, and a sharp drop in metabolism when sleeping.

steps.speaker: Options -1
options: Guess I've experienced similar things too.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Really? I had been sleeping for 57 hours straight. When I woke up, I wasn't dehydrated, hungry, or feeling anything out of the ordinary. Do you still think this is normal?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Let me put it this way. When I was asleep, I had many sweet dreams. When I woke up, all my physical functions were fine, but... my memories became jumbled.

steps.speaker: Right! No wonder it felt so familiar!
steps.content: Some bad memories became blurred and jumbled together. It took me a while to figure out what's bothering me in the first place.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: It's as if my bad memories have been squeezed out. Maybe it's not the best metaphor, but it does feel like they've been "squeezed" out.

steps.speaker: [New Clue]
steps.content: These are typical Sleepwalker symptoms.

steps.speaker: Yanyan and Greta keep on chatting. Yanyan even performs another part of the Sun Crow ritual dance in front of the crowd.
steps.content: I'm not sure. The only change in my life during that time was switching sleep meds.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: I rely on sleep meds a lot. When I become resistant to one type of meds, I switch to another. Someone recommended me a new type a while back, so I tried it out. How do I put it... the effect was outstanding.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: I'm really ashamed that as a doctor, I developed drug dependence. If it hadn't been so hard to get those meds back then, I don't know how I would've turned out.

steps.speaker: Options -1
options: Does it happen to all Sleepwalkers?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: I think so. Different people seem to have different levels of resistance to it. I'm one of the lucky ones. Those with weaker wills are more affected.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Ha. If they really did something to me, I would have been sent to the detection station by now. This isn't Syndicate. It's harder to see a Sinner than to shake hands with the head of the Council.
If he had come up the stairs, he'd probably already seen the two downstairs.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: I know what you're thinking, but my situation has nothing to do with Mania.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Even if you include my patients, my social circle is quite small. I haven't met any Sinners, and the alarms in District 14 haven't gone off for a long time.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: I haven't seen any black goo, let alone Sinners. My M-value has always been within normal range.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: You're very safe.
From his repeated emphasis, it does seem that Eastsiders are extremely wary of Mania.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Do you guys have any more questions?
The bait has been thrown, but Inspector Doyle just buries his head in the cushion and acts like he doesn't care. You take over the conversation.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I'm quite interested in the sleeping meds you mentioned.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If they're really that powerful, there must be a lot of rumors about them in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: You're right, there are a lot of rumors about it. Maybe you've heard of the name... <color=#fb9259>Ambrosia</color>. True to its name, it's a heavenly new drink.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Very sweet.
It's indeed a familiar name.
Before you can recall all the details, Doyle sits up.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: Holy ****, Gandall! Why didn't you say this earlier?!

steps.speaker: Gandall
steps.content: I told you this last week, inspector. You didn't pay attention.
Doyle slaps his head hard, staggers onto his feet, and puts on an old coat.

steps.speaker: Doyle
steps.content: I heard this name recently. I know where to buy this stuff.

steps.speaker: Gandall
steps.content: So the incredible inspector finally found his groove again?
Doyle doesn't reply. Ignoring Gandall, he strides to the door and swings it open.
Clang!
